Fogbank moss

Fogbank moss is an invented plant, written for this fixture so that the page carries real prose without reproducing anyone else's. It is described here as a low cushion-forming species of temperate coastal headlands, where it draws most of its water from sea fog rather than from rainfall.

The cushions are said to grow no more than four centimetres tall and to spread outward at the margins while dying back at the centre, so that an old colony reads as a ring rather than a disc. Nothing in this paragraph is a claim about the world; it exists to give the text, links, and accessibility views something ordinary to render.
